_note: Fact sheets (prompt §11.5; docs/research/power-costs-outcomes.md §3-6, sites.md §3). Each row carries its quote and source key. Rows with `fx` get approxUsd computed by 60_curated.py from the FRED annual averages in `fxRates` and are labelled 'approx.'.

sheets.title: What a lunar landing attempt costs

rows.label: Headline
rows.value: A single lunar landing attempt typically costs on the order of $100 million.
rows.quote: Order-of-magnitude statement supported by Beresheet (~$100M), Peregrine ($107.9M task order) and IM-1 ($122.0M task order); counter-examples: Chandrayaan-3 (~$30M excl. launch) and IM-2 PRIME-1 ($50.0M).
rows.note: Not a rule: costs range from about $30M to about $140M among documented attempts.

rows.label: Beresheet (2019, crashed)
rows.quote: The mission cost about $100 million
rows.note: Includes launch; press figure.

rows.label: Chandrayaan-2 project (2019; lander crashed, orbiter succeeded)
rows.quote: approved cost ... Rs. 603 Crore (excluding launch cost)
rows.note: Includes the orbiter.

rows.label: Chandrayaan-2 launch vehicle (GSLV Mk III M1)
rows.quote: GSLV MK III M1 vehicle is Rs. 367 Crore

rows.label: Chandrayaan-3 (2023, success)
rows.quote: The approved cost of Chandrayaan-3 is Rs. 250 Crores (Excluding Launch Vehicle Cost)

rows.label: SLIM total development (2024, landed in wrong attitude)
rows.quote: Total project development cost 14.9 billion yen
rows.note: About $106M at the 2023 rate; budget at project start was ¥18.05B.

rows.label: Peregrine Mission One (2024, never reached the Moon)
rows.quote: OIG Table 2: Astrobotic TO2-AB, $79.5M initial, $107.9M current task order value
rows.note: NASA task-order (delivery) value, not the full mission cost to the vendor.

rows.label: IM-1 Odysseus (2024, landed and tipped)
rows.quote: CLPS paid Intuitive Machines about $122 million
rows.note: Task-order value. NASA's six IM-1 instruments cost the agency about $9.5 million.

rows.label: IM-2 PRIME-1 task order (2025, landed on its side)
rows.quote: Intuitive Machines (PRIME-1) October 2020 47.0 50.0
rows.note: Task-order value.

rows.label: Blue Ghost Mission 1 (2025, success)
rows.quote: OIG Table 2: Firefly TO19D, $93.3M initial, $101.5M current
rows.note: Task-order value.

rows.label: CLPS contract cap
rows.quote: combined maximum contract value of $2.6 billion through 2028

rows.label: 'Shots on goal'
rows.value: NASA informally refers to this risk posture as taking 'shots on goal.'
rows.quote: NASA informally refers to this risk posture as taking 'shots on goal.'
rows.note: Quoted from a 2025 House Science Committee hearing charter, not a NASA document.

rows.label: HAKUTO-R Mission 1 cost
rows.note: No cost found in an opened source; listed in docs/MISSING_DATA.md.

rows.label: Luna 25 cost
rows.note: No cost found in an opened source; listed in docs/MISSING_DATA.md.

rows.label: Tally
rows.value: 14 attempts: 5 clean soft landings, 3 landed in an unplanned attitude, 5 crashes, 1 never reached the Moon
rows.quote: Five clean soft landings (Chang'e-4, Chang'e-5, Chandrayaan-3, Chang'e-6, Blue Ghost M1). Three landed in an unplanned attitude (SLIM, IM-1, IM-2). Five crashes (Beresheet, Chandrayaan-2, HAKUTO-R M1, Luna 25, RESILIENCE). One never reached the Moon (Peregrine).
rows.note: Compiled from the sources in each row; no attempt found 26 Oct-14 Nov 2026.

rows.label: 2019-01-03 Chang'e-4
rows.quote: Far side, Von Kármán crater
rows.note: cause class: none

rows.label: 2019-04-11 Beresheet
rows.quote: A software command uploaded to fix a sensor problem started a chain reaction
rows.note: cause class: hardware-command

rows.label: 2019-09-07 IST Chandrayaan-2 Vikram
rows.quote: the reduction in velocity was more than the designed value ... Vikram hard landed within 500 m of the designated landing site
rows.note: cause class: gnc-braking (not a site or date problem)

rows.label: 2020-12-01 Chang'e-5
rows.quote: 15:11 UTC 01 December 2020
rows.note: cause class: none

rows.label: 2023-04-26 JST HAKUTO-R M1
rows.quote: simulations ... did not adequately incorporate the lunar environment on the navigation route
rows.note: cause class: terrain-software (crater rim on a changed, unsimulated route)

rows.label: 2023-08-19 Luna 25
rows.quote: operated for 127 seconds instead of 84
rows.note: cause class: propulsion-burn (pre-landing orbit)

rows.label: 2023-08-23 Chandrayaan-3
rows.quote: On 23rd Aug, 2023, Chandrayaan-3 lander, Vikram, successfully soft-landed on the Moon.
rows.note: cause class: none; did not wake after the lunar night

rows.label: 2024-01-08..18 Peregrine M1
rows.quote: operated the spacecraft for 10 days and 14 hours
rows.note: cause class: hardware-propulsion (propellant leak, helium valve)

rows.label: 2024-01-20 JST SLIM
rows.quote: nozzle separated and thrust was reduced in one of the two main engines
rows.note: cause class: hardware-propulsion; landed about 55 m from target; survived 3 lunar nights

rows.label: 2024-02-22 IM-1 Odysseus
rows.quote: their laser range finders couldn't be turned on as they had a manual safety switch turned on
rows.note: cause class: procedural-sensor; the 12° slope contributed to the tip

rows.label: 2024-06-01 Chang'e-6
rows.quote: LROC: lander at 41.6385°S, 206.0148°E
rows.note: cause class: none

rows.label: 2025-03-02 Blue Ghost M1
rows.quote: upright and stable
rows.note: cause class: none

rows.label: 2025-03-06 IM-2 Athena
rows.quote: With the direction of the sun, the orientation of the solar panels, and extreme cold temperatures in the crater, Intuitive Machines does not expect Athena to recharge
rows.note: cause class: nav-sensor + lighting/thermal at the landing spot; ended in under 13 h

rows.label: 2025-06-06 JST ispace RESILIENCE
rows.quote: deterioration in the performance ... or the performance itself was lower than expected
rows.note: cause class: sensor-hardware (laser rangefinder)

rows.label: 2026 (through 14 Nov)
rows.quote: Chang'e-7 postponed 'at least to some time next year'; Blue Moon MK1, Griffin-1, IM-3 and Blue Ghost 2 slipped to 2027.
rows.note: The Space Review checked through 26 Oct 2026; this pipeline found nothing between 26 Oct and 14 Nov 2026.

rows.label: Total solar irradiance at 1 AU
rows.quote: The most accurate value of total solar irradiance during the 2008 solar minimum period is 1360.8 ± 0.5 W m-2

rows.label: Solar irradiance (NASA fact sheet)
rows.quote: Solar irradiance (W/m2) 1361.0

rows.label: Irradiance scaling
rows.quote: Inverse-square law; r is the Sun range from the ephemeris. About ±3.4% over a year (1408 W/m2 at perihelion, 1317 at aphelion).
rows.note: derived

rows.label: Triple-junction cell efficiency (BOL)
rows.note: Bare cell, AM0, 28 °C

rows.label: Synodic month
rows.quote: Synodic period (days) 29.53

rows.label: Lunar day or night (half a synodic month)
rows.note: derived; about 354 h

rows.label: Equatorial maximum surface temperature
rows.quote: ∼387–397 K at the equator, dropping to ∼95 K just before sunrise

rows.label: Equatorial pre-dawn minimum
rows.quote: dropping to ∼95 K just before sunrise

rows.label: Polar cold trap (LCROSS site, subsurface estimate)
rows.quote: subsurface temperatures are estimated to be 38 kelvin

rows.label: Cold-trap threshold
rows.quote: Annual maximum temperature below 110 K, as used by Li et al. 2018 (filter) and Fisher et al. 2017 (reflectance transition).
rows.note: Surface ice exposures were found in only about 3.5% of cold traps (Li et al. 2018). Never call a cold trap 'ice-bearing'.

rows.label: Moon reference radius
rows.quote: Center radii : 1737.4, 1737.4, 1737.4 km (Horizons header); LOLA adopts a spherical geometry with a radius of 1737.4 km

rows.label: Artemis III
rows.value: Crewed test flight in low Earth orbit, 2027 (not a landing)
rows.quote: Artemis III is now a 2027 low-Earth-orbit test flight (rendezvous and docking with SpaceX and/or Blue Origin landers, plus xEVA suit tests).
rows.note: Restated in NASA's 23 Oct 2026 blog.

rows.label: Artemis IV
rows.quote: Launch: 'Early 2028'

rows.label: Candidate landing regions
rows.quote: the agency has identified nine candidate landing regions near the lunar South Pole
rows.note: Named on 28 Oct 2024 'in no priority order'. No coordinates or boundaries published.

rows.label: Region size and sunlight
rows.value: about 15 x 15 km; continuous sunlight over a 6.5-day period
rows.quote: All 13 regions contain sites that provide continuous access to sunlight throughout a 6.5-day period ... approximately 9.3 by 9.3 miles (15 by 15 kilometers)
rows.note: From the 2022 list of 13 regions.

rows.label: Restatement
rows.value: Artemis III LEO in 2027; Artemis IV first landing in 2028
rows.quote: Artemis III ... low Earth orbit in 2027
